correctness.rationale: For every finite commutative chain ring, simultaneous conjugation fixes the first primitive idempotent as \(E=e_{11}\). The second is uniquely \(F=\begin{psmallmatrix}t&b\\c&1-t\end{psmallmatrix}\) with \(bc=t(1-t)\). Four Peirce corners generate exactly the order with unrestricted diagonal entries and off-diagonal ideals \((b)\) and \((c)\). Its additive index exponent is \(\nu(b)+\nu(c)\). If \(bc\) is in the maximal ideal, the quadratic equation has exactly two simple lifted roots; when both are units a separate direct count applies. This proves every coefficient, normalization and all-length and all-characteristic claims. Exact sums prove the total-variation limiting tail and quadratic expected index. Nine exhaustive finite-ring enumerations and selected generated-span computations passed. The experiments do not replace the proof and no result outside finite commutative chain rings is claimed.

originality.rationale: The original component is the complete valuation-pair/index-fiber census of two primitive idempotents over every finite commutative chain ring, its product-of-ideal-chains order spectrum, and the tight-versus-quadratic asymptotic contrast. Rowen–Segev establishes the general structural two-idempotent theorem and the classical generation criterion; neither the field-generation problem nor the known q=2 obstruction is claimed as novel. Their theorem does not state or dominate this local-valuation enumeration. The closest published finite-field generation census has no variable chain length or positive valuation indices. value.rationale: The entire index distribution of R-subalgebras generated by two primitive idempotents is a natural matrix-algebra generation invariant; it distinguishes each pair of Peirce off-diagonal ideals, gives the exact attainable-order poset, works across equal and mixed characteristic, and establishes a nontrivial tight-log-index versus quadratically divergent expected-index dichotomy. It is not just the known two-idempotent generation event, a narrow numerical sample, or a textbook substitute for Rowen–Segev.
